title: Signal-Driven Canary Dashboard & Quick-Rollback Flow
creator: Alex Navarro
description: Design and prototype a compact dashboard and interaction flow that lets operators run signal-driven canary launches, observe key telemetry, and execute a one-click rollback or fast-fail routing change. Focus is on surfacing automated signal thresholds, clear time-windowed metrics, and a minimal incident-safe rollback pathway suitable for both Hosted and Dedicated deployments.
goals: Expose real-time canary signal indicators (latency, error-rate, token cost delta) in a single glance
Enable policy-driven auto-pause and human-triggered rollback with clear audit trail
Design a compact timeline visual that shows traffic split, rollout ramp, and decision points
Support quick fallback actions that are reversible and include confirmation affordances for safety
non_goals: Ship full backend orchestration for rollouts (this ticket is UX + spec only)
Replace existing long-form Rollouts page — this is an opportunistic companion dashboard for high-risk launches
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma prototype of dashboard and rollback modal linked in attachments
Usability walkthrough with at least two platform engineers and one SRE; changes addressed in design
Clear copy for all safety states (auto-paused, degraded, healthy) and one-click rollback confirmation copy finalized
Hand-off spec with component list, accessibility notes, and telemetry keys required by backend team
progress_updates: 2025-02-05: Kickoff with PM and runtime eng. Agreed scope: dashboard is read-only for canary metrics; quick actions will call an existing rollout API (ENG-3842)
2025-02-07: Low-fidelity flows sketched. Decision: show three primary signals by default (p50 latency, 95th latency, error-rate) and collapsed advanced signals
2025-02-09: Iteration after SRE review: added an auto-pause indicator and explicit timestamp of last evaluation to avoid implicit staleness
2025-02-12: Prototype updated with fast-rollback modal and audit confirmation step. PM requested inclusion of cost-delta metric for signal correlation
2025-02-14: Design critique with frontend: confirmed component constraints and agreed on animation budget for timeline scrub to reduce perceived delay
review_feedback: PM (Leah Kim) 2025-02-08: Like the signal badges; asks for clearer mapping between thresholds and recommended action
SRE (Marcus T.) 2025-02-09: Wants the rollback action to show the previous stable variant and an ETA for traffic stabilization
Frontend (Jordan L.) 2025-02-12: Concern about overfetching telemetry; suggested server-side aggregation of 1-minute windows
Eng lead (Ravi Shah) 2025-02-13: Requested an extra safety interstitial when rollback would cross account-level quotas
design_decisions: Surface only three primary signals in the main card to reduce cognitive load; advanced signals live in an expandable panel
Use color-safe badges and concise microcopy for states: Healthy / Degraded / Auto-paused / Rolling-back
Rollback is modeled as a reversible routing change: immediate traffic shift + 30s soft-grace window to cancel
Timeline scrub is non-blocking and visual-only; exact time-series data fetched on demand to limit backend load
accessibility_notes: All signal badges provide text equivalents and aria-live updates for screen readers
Rollback confirmation dialog follows WCAG contrast and provides keyboard-only flow with clear focus management
handoff_artifacts: Component inventory (icons, badges, timeline, modal, confirmation CTA) included in Figma
Telemetry keys and threshold names documented in Confluence page
Frontend implementation checklist with API endpoints: /rollouts/{id}/actions, /telemetry/{rollout_id}/summary
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Operators may over-rely on single signal; Mitigation: show correlation panel with cost and quality metrics side-by-side
Risk: Fast rollback could create traffic oscillation; Mitigation: introduce a 30s soft-grace cancel window and rate-limited rollback ops
Risk: Telemetry lag leading to stale decisions; Mitigation: show explicit 'last evaluated' timestamp and degrade visual confidence after 2m

02/19: Finalize Figma and export component tokens for frontend

notes_for_engineering: Preferred default traffic display is percent with small absolute counts (e.g., 12% — ~1.2k reqs/min)
Telemetry aggregation should support 1m, 5m, 15m windows; default to 1m for canary views
Rollback API should return a suggested alternate variant id and a dry-run preview of traffic distribution
